La Nucia (km 18.1) was home to Spain’s national championships in 2021. Omar Fraile won the men’s elite title ahead of Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH). Mavi Garcia won the women’s title. And Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) was crowned ahead of Marcel Camprubi (Pinarello Q36.5) in the men’s U23 race.
Coll de Rates is an emblematic ascent of the area, where dozens of professionals and amateurs rate their climbing abilities almost on a daily basis. It is also a classic on the roads of the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana, and has featured several times in La Vuelta, most recently in 2016 en route to Alto de Aitana.
The race skirts around Benidorm, a classic venue of La Vuelta, who notably hosted the Gran Salida on three occasions (1964, 1987, 2011). Benidorm also hosted the road world championships in 1992.
Since 2023, Benidorm is home to a cyclo-cross world cup round. Wout van Aert won the men’s elite race in 2024 and Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek) succeeded him 2025. Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) has also participated in the event several times as a junior and U23 rider.
Benidorm is also the hometown of Hector Alvarez, among Spain’s biggest talents.
